summary.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
summary.overview:
Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.</overview>

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.
